messages.author: 9d7c257e609d0807
messages.subject: Re: [Israel RUG] change content of list using lapply
parts:
To the best of my knowledge and experience (which means not much), R is a functional language, which means that arguments to the functions cannot be changed.
Given that under the hood, most of R is written in C, there must be a way to pass arguments by reference, and then change them - However, I wouldn't recommend it.

by the way, even your simple code does not really change the list. at least in my R version (2.11.1 on ubuntu) - the test list is the same after the call to sapply.

in a functional language, the only way to change the value of a variable is to assign a new value to it (or to part of it) within its scope. the "no side effects" principle is important in functional languages, and it has both benefits and drawbacks - but it iw what it is.

I hope this helps

Amit

messages.subject: Re: [Israel RUG] change content of list using lapply
parts:
A simple change in the code you supplied will do the work:
test = list(list(a=1,b=2),list(a=3,c=4))
test = lapply(test,function(x) {x$a=15;x})
test

other methods may be to use unlist/relist (and change the unlisted vector before the relist), or change the way you implement your data model. for example, convert your list of lists or part of it, into a data frame, and then change a column instantly.

messages.subject: Re: [Israel RUG] change content of list using lapply
parts:
The beginning of a solution: Ladies and gentlemen I give you - Environments! (I think aka namespaces)

By evaluating an expression (the R equivalent of pointers) you can change a variable outside the scope of the function. Very convenient when you do not want to pass huge data frames from function to function but keep a single copy in memory and change it.


For example:
=========

change_test = function(place, val) {
   eval(
      parse(text = paste('test[[', place, ']]$a = ', value, sep = '')), 
      envir = globalenv()
   )
}

change_test(1,15) #note that the function returns nothing
test  # the original variable is changes

No, you have to do some digging into sapply to find out exactly what variable names are passed to the applied function, because expression are practically string command you execute (try eval(parse(text = 'non_existing_variable')) to see) - so they are very sensitive to names.

Happy digging!

Yizhar

messages.subject: Re: [Israel RUG] change content of list using lapply
parts:
Sadly, lapply is an "internal" R function so I'm not sure how you can combine using expressions and environments with sapply directly.

I think the direction should be:

test<- list(list(a=10),list(a=11))

lapply(1:length(test), function(place, value = 15) {eval(parse(text = paste('test[[', place, ']]$a = ', value, sep = '')), envir = globalenv())}) # returns something but who cares...

test # the original variable is altered

for multiple value changes I think there's mapply or one of the other variants

(and sorry for the horrible spelling/grammar mistakes before, I hope you got the point I was trying to make)


Yizhar
